findings.evidence: Timing defaults, adjustable for urgency, availability, and topic: private, 30-45 minutes, at a point where both people can follow up within a day or two.
findings.fix: Remove the generic private, 30-45 minutes advice, which the model already gives. Keep only the non-obvious rule: before a weekend, leave or long absence, arrange named support and book the follow-up in the same conversation.

findings.evidence: Give logistics (dates, contacts, next steps) in writing as well: people in shock do not retain spoken detail.
findings.fix: Fold this into the Section 8 summary template as a 'Logistics handed over' line instead of restating standard bad-news practice the model already knows.

findings.evidence: ## 4. Delivering a decision is four unordered bullets with no sequence
findings.fix: Number the steps so the order is explicit: 1) confirm the approved reason and process with HR; 2) state the decision in the first two sentences; 3) name what the person can still influence; 4) hand over written logistics and book the follow-up. This matches the numbered procedure in Section 3.

findings.evidence: Never let readiness become indefinite postponement. A dated pause is regulation; an open one is avoidance.
findings.fix: This repeats the Section 2 rule on line 25. Replace it with a new landmine, for example: 'Never ask for a raise at the review meeting itself: calibration inputs are already fixed weeks earlier, so the answer is decided before you speak.'

findings.evidence: Use for compensation, promotion or workload negotiation, delivering a role elimination or other bad news, ...
findings.fix: Prepare, rehearse and follow up on high-stakes workplace conversations where the outcome is negotiated, facts are disputed, the news is bad, or emotions may derail it. Use for asking for a raise, salary, promotion or workload terms; delivering a layoff, role elimination or other bad news; a clash after public criticism or a blowup; mediating a dispute between others whose accounts conflict; raising a sensitive personal concern, harassment, or threats at work; deciding whether you are calm enough to talk; or repairing after getting defensive, even if the user never says 'difficult conversation'. Not for feedback on a specific behavior (including to each person in a conflict you lead), recognition, replying to vague criticism, scope or deadline pushback, or feedback recaps (use feedback-mastery); not for legal advice, drafting formal complaints, PIPs, ratings, policy, or company-wide announcements.

findings.evidence: name an HR, trusted management, union, ethics, or alternate reporting channel
findings.fix: Set a default and an escape hatch: 'Default to HR. If HR or the normal manager is implicated, use the ethics hotline or a skip-level manager. Add the union rep when the user is covered.'

findings.evidence: "Provides a neutral opening using an I-statement or collaborative intent"
findings.fix: Base the assertion on what the skill teaches (Section 5): 'Opening names the situation, observable behavior, impact, and ends with an open question inviting their account'. Also add evals for a role-elimination delivery (decision in the first two sentences, approved reason only) and for repair after getting defensive.

findings.evidence: The routing table has no row for 'raising a sensitive personal concern', which the description and trigger query 'tell my manager about a health issue' both claim
findings.fix: Add a routing row: 'Raising a sensitive personal matter (health, family) | Section 5 opening, impact-on-work only | delivery-scripts.md sensitive-matter line'. Also widen the delivery-scripts.md gate so it covers this route.

findings.evidence: For role eliminations and other HR-led decisions, use only the approved reason and HR's process
findings.fix: Add a fallback for when there is no HR function or no approved wording yet: 'If no approved reason exists, do not deliver; get the wording agreed in writing with whoever owns the decision (founder, legal counsel) first.'

findings.evidence: Readiness never delays urgent safety or operational matters: those go to timely support now (Section 7).
findings.fix: Section 7 covers only safety and misconduct, so operational matters have nowhere to go. Name the route for urgent operational issues (for example, 'raise it now with the decision owner, keep it to facts, and defer the relationship conversation to a dated slot'), or drop 'operational' from the sentence.
